notes:
Summary: Aurora Codex Labs builds an in-IDE copilot for enterprise dev teams (VS Code + JetBrains plugins). Primary ask: deterministic, reproducible code completions with model/version pinning and safe rollouts. They need sub-100ms median completion latency for single-line completions and predictable tail latency for streaming completions.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-02-18: Product demo + architecture walk (Fireflies ff_2026-02-18_aurora-poc-demo). AE/SE: Jordan + Priya. Positive reaction to Redwood's routing + canary features.
- 2026-02-24: Security intake kickoff (shared security FAQ link). Customer provided SOC2 + ISO requirements.
- 2026-03-03: POC deploy v0 on Dedicated (small pool) — observed flaky completions when KV cache warmed on large buffers. SE triaging. Jira RDW-11234 opened.
- 2026-03-10: Eval harness run: custom prompt-suite (500 prompts) comparing model-A@v1.2 (quant-8) vs model-A@v1.3 (quant-8 + kernel changes). Measured completion correctness, compile-time errors, and token-level hallucination rate.

Key requirements / notes from calls:
- Model/version pinning: must pin exact model artifact + compile profile (example: model-a:v1.3+q8+cuda-kernel-2). Any rollout must be able to specify canary % and deterministic routing by user/team.
- Reproducibility: runs used for internal failure analysis need to be reproducible - deterministic seed + model/build id recorded in logs and accessible via API.
- Eval gates: automated guardrails required — fail rollout if syntax-correctness drops >2% or if avg edit-distance increases beyond threshold. Want ability to run pre-deploy eval suite on candidate model variants.
- Rollouts & canaries: prefer staged canary (5% internal => 20% beta teams => 100%), automatic rollback on eval-gate failures. Need per-route rollouts (IDE completions vs refactor assistant).
- Low-latency streaming: streaming token latency target: median <50ms, p95 <150ms for single-line completions. Customer is sensitive to p99s for large file contexts.
- Cache behavior: caching must not surface stale completions across pinned model variants; need prefix-aware KV caching and ability to clear caches when rolling variant.
- Observability: debug trace linking request -> model version -> kernel selection + compiler flags. Token-level cost and latency breakdown per request required for opt-in telemetry.

POC plan / milestones:
- Week 0 (this week): Deploy dedicated pool in VPC, enable model pinning beta. Run smoke tests.
- Week 1: Internal canary (5% of internal dev traffic). Collect eval metrics and logs.
- Week 2: Expand to 20% across beta org, run full eval harness nightly and compare to baseline.
- Week 3: Security sign-off and procurement finalization. Go-live target: 2026-06 (forecast).

Open questions we asked Aurora to confirm:
- Exact tolerance thresholds for eval gates (they suggested 2% syntax drop, 1% latency increase allowed).
- Whether they require HSM-backed key storage vs cloud KMS for private deployment.
- If they want to pin quantization profile or allow automatic fallback to higher-precision variant under heavy load.

Sales notes / strategy:
- Position Redwood Dedicated + Private combo: Dedicated for predictable latency in dev stage, Private (VPC/on-prem) for data residency and compliance. Emphasize rollouts/canary primitives and built-in eval gates as differentiators vs managed endpoints from competitors.
- Engineering ask: SE to deliver a short reproducibility checklist and an example eval-gate config YAML by next call.

Next step (short): Priya to deliver sample canary config + eval-suite template; Jordan to schedule security follow-up the week of 2026-03-15.

Customer quote (paraphrase): "We need to be sure an upgrade won't silently nudge completions and break CI — reproducible runs and rollback must be atomic."
